text:
All tests pass and the issue's example now correctly raises `CycleError: dependency cycle among ['x', 'y']`.

**Root cause:** The cycle detection compared `len(result)` against `len(graph)` — the number of *keys* in the input dict — instead of the full node set. Nodes that appear only as dependencies (like `lib`, `util`, `log`) are also part of the graph, so when the acyclic portion contributed more nodes than the number of keys, the count check `len(result) < len(graph)` could pass even though cycle members (`x`, `y`) were never emitted. A pure two-node cycle has no such extra nodes, which is why it was reported correctly.

**Fix:** One line in `deps/graph.py` — compare against `len(deps)`, the complete node set (keys plus dependency-only names), which is also what the error message already uses.
